transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-22 16:00 UTC / Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis & Jamal (Redwood SEs), Sarah (RidgePoint Head of Data & Privacy), Priya (Security Architect), Tom (Platform), Evan (Legal)

Summary: Short intake to understand RidgePoint's controls road map and decide between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for production ML inference. Main concerns: customer key control (KMS/HSM), SOC2 and ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration, audit logs and retention/erasures, data residency and legal hold for payments-related PII.

Topics: SOC 2/ISO requirements; SSO/SAML/SCIM for SSO; RBAC mapping to internal roles; audit logs format/retention; encryption at rest/in transit; KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed); private VPC/on-prem tradeoffs; data retention & deletion requests; bench test to validate tokenization and KV cache behavior.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE, and with me are Luis and Jamal from solutions.
[00:10] Sarah: Hi, Sarah Li here. I'm leading data/privacy at RidgePoint. We're trying to lock down approach for inference for our new payments flows.
[00:20] Tom: Tom, platform eng, I'll be running any infra proofs of concept.
[00:24] Priya: Priya, security architect. We'll be the primary reviewers of the controls.
[00:30] Maya: Great. The goal today is to map your compliance requirements to our hosting options — Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved pools vs Private VPC/on-prem. Also KMS, audit, retention.
[00:42] Luis: Quick note: when we say "Dedicated" it's dedicated GPU pools, but there's still a Redwood control plane unless you opt for Private. So key questions are whether you need customer-managed keys and full network isolation.
[00:55] Sarah: Our compliance checklist is strict: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 in progress, SSO via SAML + SCIM for provisioning, RBAC enforcement to mirror our internal roles, and audit trails with retention for 7 years for payments.
[01:10] Evan: And legal hold — we need ability to freeze or export logs for e-discovery.
[01:18] Jamal: Understood. A couple clarifying Qs: do you need model artifacts to be stored on-prem, or is it okay for weights to be hosted?
[01:27] Priya: Prefer weights outside public multi-tenant; we want control over keys at minimum and ideally HSM for KMS. If not possible, we need cryptographic separation and audited key usage.
[01:40] Luis: We support customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS integrations (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) and can integrate with HSM-backed keys if you run in Private. With Dedicated you can bring-your-own-key but network controls are less strict than Private.
[01:55] Tom: What about logs — what's collected by Redwood? We need structured audit logs of request metadata but need to avoid storing full PII or raw prompt data for longer than retention window.
[02:07] Maya: We have token-level telemetry and per-request metadata — by default Hosted retains logs for 30 days, Dedicated can be configured longer, and Private lets you control retention fully. We also offer prefix/KV cache which can reduce repeated token sending, but that cache can contain derived context so must be considered for retention.
[02:30] Sarah: We heard mention of "prefix cache" — will that store identifiers? We need to ensure that anything that could re-identify a user gets purged on request.
[02:38] Luis: Good point. Cache entries can be redacted or encrypted; on Private you can configure cache encryption with your keys. On Dedicated we can enable encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys, but full purge APIs are an opt-in feature.
[02:55] Sarah: So can you support deletion-by-identifier for logs and cache? We have GDPR and PCI-SSO-like deletion requests.
[03:05] Jamal: We have deletion APIs but with Hosted there is a standard retention lifecycle. For Dedicated/Private we can expose endpoints or playbooks for redaction and legal hold. We'll need to lock that in for your legal review.
[03:20] Priya: On SSO: can Redwood integrate with our SAML IdP and push groups via SCIM? We need SCIM provisioning and SAML for login, plus support for certificate rotation and JIT provisioning in certain cases.
[03:33] Maya: Yes, we support SAML SSO + SCIM for group sync. RBAC mappings are configurable in the Console, and we can map SAML assertions to roles. There is an admin role, dev role, observability role, etc.
[03:45] Tom: Does RBAC tie into the audit logs? We need traceability that shows which user initiated a request for forensics.
[03:52] Luis: Audit logs include actor identity when requests are made via API tokens linked to user/service accounts. For internal routing we also surface the route/model and token usage. There are caveats if you're doing token pooling for high throughput.
[04:10] Sarah: KMS specifics: customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed. For compliance we prefer customer-managed keys with HSM. Is there extra latency or cost?
[04:19] Luis: HSM-backed keys add minimal latency to key unwrap operations; we've measured a few ms on KMS calls. There's also additional throughput considerations if you perform per-request encryption operations. For the actual model serving path we keep data encrypted at rest and in transit; keys are used for disk encryption and secret wrapping.
[04:40] Sarah: Can you give example architecture for Dedicated with customer keys?
[04:45] Jamal: (shares link in chat) We'll send a diagram. High level: model weights on encrypted volumes, KMS rotates and unwraps at node boot, request path uses ephemeral session keys, logs flow to your SIEM via secure forwarder, admin plane can be placed into your VPC for Private offering.
[05:05] Evan: Regarding artifacts: we will need SOC 2 Type II report, encryption attestations, and recent pentest. Also want to see RBAC config screenshots and API for log export.
[05:20] Maya: Happy to share SOC 2 and pen test summary. I'll attach those in our follow-up.
[05:26] Priya: What about data residency? We need primary region in us-east-1 and failover in eu-west-1 — any cross-region replication concerns?
[05:36] Luis: We can pin workloads to regions and enable cross-region replication only if you enable it. For Hosted we have multi-region failover; for Dedicated you can request region pinning; Private gives you full control.
[05:50] Sarah: There's a specific ask from compliance: can we audit KMS usage logs to verify key access per request?
[05:59] Luis: Yes, both cloud KMS and HSM vendors provide audit logs; we can surface key usage events in our audit trails or push them to your logging endpoint. We'll include examples.
[06:15] Tom: Bench testing: we want to run a POC to validate tokenization and KV cache behavior under our sample payloads. Can Redwood run a bench showing exact token counts, latency and cache hit rates?
[06:28] Jamal: Yes, we can run bench tests. We'll need a sample prompt set and representative seq lengths. We usually run tests on Dedicated pools but can emulate on Hosted for small sets.
[06:40] Priya: About legal hold: if we need to freeze logs for an investigation, how is that handled?
[06:47] Maya: We have a legal-hold process where we can snapshot logs and disable automated deletion, but for Hosted there are constraints; Dedicated or Private are much more flexible.
[06:58] Sarah: Any compliance red flags you often see with payments customers?
[07:04] Luis: Common ones: storing raw PANs or full cardholder data in prompts, lack of tokenization at the app layer, and assuming default retention is compliant. We always recommend removing sensitive data at the application boundary and using tokenization or hashing before hitting the model.
[07:22] Tom: Do you support field-level redaction in the request pipeline?
[07:27] Jamal: We support pre-processing hooks and recommend pre-tokenization at app layer. For Private deployments you can run a pre-filter in your VPC.
[07:36] Priya: On certificates and rotation: we need to rotate keys every 90 days and support emergency rotation. Is that possible?
[07:43] Luis: Yes, recommended pattern is KMS rotation plus secret manager for credentials. For customer-managed KMS, rotation policies live on your side; we can coordinate and support zero-downtime key swaps.
[07:59] Evan: For our legal team — Do you provide retention policy templates and runbooks for data subject requests?
[08:06] Maya: Yes, we have runbooks and can adapt them. We'll include a sample retention policy and deletion playbook.
[08:15] Sarah: Ok, quick price sensitivity: Dedicated is more expensive but offers stronger isolation. Private likely requires a license. If we have to keep HSM and private control plane, that's heavier.
[08:28] Maya: Correct. We'll include cost delta estimates in the follow-up pricing.
[08:34] Tom: We need to know what artifacts you can provide for our procurement security questionnaire.
[08:39] Maya: SOC 2 report, ISO scoping info, pen test summary, diagram, and some RBAC screenshots. We'll attach these.
[08:48] Priya: Also need to validate API tokens lifecycle and secrets management best practices — e.g., short-lived tokens and rotation.
[08:56] Luis: We support short-lived tokens via our auth system and integration with your identity provider for service accounts.
[09:05] Sarah: Great. Any other gotchas? For example, is there any telemetry that might leak production data into vendor metrics?
[09:13] Jamal: By default we collect aggregated telemetry; raw request payloads are used for debugging only and access is limited. We can disable storage of raw prompts or encrypt them with your keys in Private.
[09:28] Maya: Recap / next steps: we'll send SOC 2 artifacts, network/arch diagrams, KMS patterns, and a proposed schedule for bench testing. You'll provide security questionnaire and sample prompts. We'll schedule a follow-up technical bench session with Jamal and Tom.
[09:45] Sarah: Sounds good. Priya will coordinate with Tom on sample data. Evan will follow up on legal hold language.
[09:54] Evan: One more thing — SLA expectations for Dedicated: need uptime and latency SLOs in contract; can you share standard SLA?
[10:04] Luis: Yes, Dedicated has SLA options; we'll include the SLA docs. Private is handled via license agreement with enterprise terms.
[10:16] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and propose times for the bench test.
[10:22] Sarah: Thanks, bye.

(Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings. There were a few moments of crosstalk when network diagrams were being discussed. Links shared in chat: network-arch-diagram.png, SOC2-summary.pdf, KMS-integration-recommendation.md)
